title: Pay to win
body:
It’s a great app and I definitely recommend it to anyone who is motivated by gamification. It’s a little confusing to navigate at first, but great once you get the hang of it. However if you want to collect all the pets and such, you have no choice but to subscribe. Pet quests can be gained if you join a party with people who have subscriptions, but for pets that can’t be obtained through quests you’re basically screwed. Challenges can give you gem rewards, but chances of winning are very slim. I would love if gems were purchasable with coins but were very expensive per gem to encourage people to either grind for them or subscribe. 
That being said I can see how that could be abused with FCV and spamming habits, so if that were implemented those things would need to be adjusted and capped. But I do think it’s doable and less scammy, and honestly a more motivating option. I’ve fallen off Habitica a lot because when those things are unattainable there’s little incentive to actually use the app
TL;DR: Good app overall but in my opinion the motivating factors are not sustainable. Claims not to be a pay to win game but absolutely is one if you want to collect things, which is the main reward system of the game. Needs adjustments

title: Good For Helping Me Improve, But Very Buggy!
body:
I have been using the app for nearly two years, and I have been able to steadily increase the number of tasks and frequency at which I do them. In that respect, I find the app very helpful for my ADHD.

However the app is extremely buggy. At least once a week, the app will tell me it started a new day, but it hasn’t cleared out my dailies from the previous day. I then can’t log my tasks for the current day until something about the server resets and finally refreshes so I can log my tasks.

Also, regardless of all the other improvements that have been made in the app, a glaring issue is that pressing the “+” button beside a task will not add the point to the task I selected, but to a completely different task. The haptic tracking is very off. It’s extremely frustrating that I have to tap the “+” to add points every time, I can’t just type it in. When my method of using the app is assigning points based on how hard the task is for me on a given day (sometimes my chronic pain conditions make a task much more difficult than on a different day), I have to repeatedly tap the “+” button to add those points that day. Sometimes I give myself 100 points for cleaning the toilet or doing the dishes, and having to press the button 100 times is so aggravating when the number glitches and adds some of the points elsewhere instead.

Can this be addressed in an upcoming update, please? The haptic feedback badly needs adjusting. Some days these bugs are so bad, I don’t even want to use the app at all.

author: SunflowerValentine

title: Moving in the WRONG direction!!!!
body:
⭐☆☆☆☆

I realize I’m late to this news, but I just rediscovered Habitica after using it consistently from 2020 through 2023 — and I genuinely cannot believe the guilds are gone.

The guilds were the soul of this app. That’s not dramatic — that’s accurate. They were how I found goal-specific communities, niche challenges, accountability partners, and like-minded people pushing toward the same achievements. Whether it was fitness, language learning, productivity sprints, or life resets, guilds created momentum. They made change feel communal instead of lonely.

Coming back, I was actually excited. I thought, “Okay, let’s see what guilds are active now. Let’s plug back in.” And they just… don’t exist. That completely deflates the experience. The app without guilds feels like a stripped-down habit tracker with RPG cosmetics. Functional? Sure. Inspiring? Not even close.

What makes this more frustrating is the subscription fee. You’re charging $4.99/month. If moderation was the issue, raise the price. Gate guild access behind subscription. Recruit paid moderators. Build a scaled-down version. There were options. Eliminating them entirely feels like removing the engine because maintaining it was inconvenient.

I understand this happened a while ago. I’m just rediscovering the app now, and the downgrade hits hard. The excitement, the optimism, the sense of shared transformation — gone. For an app built around gamified self-improvement, removing the primary social motivation system feels like a massive strategic misstep.

Really disappointing.

title: Helpful, but actual fun content is hidden behind a paywall
body:
Habitica has 2 currencies: gems and coins. Coins you can get for free by doing tasks but gems are mostly given via the monthly subscription, they CAN be gotten for free however it’s insanely tedious

Gems are basically where all the actually fun stuff for the game is hidden. The quests and many customization items are stuck behind gem paywalls, so without them or a person in your party thst has premium and can buy the party quests, the game is just boring grinding with basically no real end goal

The way to get gems for free is also flawed, the only ways are website giveaways or challenges, which will give you tasks and is basically gambling. You join challenges, complete tasks, and have a random chance of getting selected to win gems. This however completely ruins the betterment aspect of the game as since it’s literally just gambling, you’re pushed to join as many challenges as you can physically handle, and to actually have a good chance at getting gems, you have to just lie and say you did it. It’s the only real way to get any. Plus, completing challenges gives you in game coins, which when you’re forced to lie about it basically just gives you free money and ruins any actual habit building.

In all, fine game, bad way of dealing with the ptw currency. Personally, I believe small amounts of gems should be given to you if you go on habitica daily, like 1 per month, and the longer your streak gets, the more gems you’re given. It’d still make gems annoying to get for free players (2 months for a single hair color) and keep players keeping up their habits naturally while still being able to do fun activities like quests.

title: Pomodoro Timer (HabiFocus) request
body:
Dear Habitica Team,

I’m writing to submit a feature request for a built-in Habitica-themed Pomodoro timer (HabiFocus)—a tool that would gamify focus sessions and tie directly into Habitica’s core RPG/task system, boosting productivity for the community while staying true to the app’s fun, quest-based vibe.

Core Concept for HabiFocus

The timer would align with the classic Pomodoro method and integrate seamlessly with Habitica’s existing rewards/mechanics:

• A 25-minute HabiFocus work session = earn a small Gold reward

• A 5-minute HabiRest break 

• 4 completed HabiFocus cycles = a HabiVictory long break, plus a random Loot drop (e.g., potions, eggs) as a bonus reward

Why This Matters for Habitica

This feature would bridge the gap between focus and task completion—something many users already try to do with third-party Pomodoro tools—by making productivity a native part of the Habitica experience. It would enhance the app’s core value of turning daily habits into a fun quest, and appeal to students, remote workers, and anyone using Habitica to build consistent focus routines.

I think this timer would be a fantastic addition to Habitica’s existing features, and I’d love to see how the team could refine the mechanics to fit the app’s world. Please let me know if you need any additional details or feedback from the community to develop this idea further!

Thank you for all the hard work you put into making Habitica such a wonderful, motivating tool for building better habits. I’m excited to see the app grow and evolve.
author: Feature update Jan-31

title: The idea has limitless potential but the execution is awful
body: There's so many ways that this idea could be good, but clearly the devs just stopped at "good enough." I just want an app that makes creating a routine fun, and I love rpg's so I figured this would be a real winner. I'm assuming the dev is like 50+ years old and never actually played a real rpg video game from this era. My guess is that they spend  99% of their time playing D&D, because all rpg elements are clearly inspired by it. It'd also explain the choice of 1980's graphics. When I finally got to go on my first quest, I thought "finally, something to do other than collecting useless items" but I was quickly back to being disappointed. Like D&D, you have to imagine going on a quest. Why there's not actually any real monsters to fight with your character is beyond me. There's also absolutely no purpose in any of the classes. Nothing changes from being a rogue or a mage, the entire class system is arbitrary. It's basically this: want more useless items, pick a rogue, want more useless experience points, pick a mage, etc. The only thing that resembles anything like a video game rpg is the HP and damage system. Don't do a task on your list, take damage. Ultimately, I'm deciding to uninstall this app because there's no way to interact with it on the apple watch. The habit/task tracking is good, I'm just not interested in collecting useless junk and pointless pets that do nothing. So, I might as well just switch to a normal tracker that has some apple watch capabilities.

body:
My friends and I use this to stay motivated and keep each other accountable. I know it’s just an RPG that can easily be cheated, but somehow we don’t want to cheat and the game keeps us engaged. Just bought an annual subscription which I rarely do for apps.

Easily 5/5 stars from me because of how effective it has been for me, but to be honest and transparent I think this app should get 4/5 stars because of a severe limitation: lack of an offline mode and robust syncing. I know it’s a hard problem but Dropbox figured out syncing almost 20 years ago, and rival task management app Things has had robust cloud (and local!) syncing for many years now.

Other things I’d like to see:
-More task management features. To Do’s seems to be the weakest of the three main lists. You can do almost anything with combinations of hashtags and filtering but it’s clumsy. I use only Habitica for habit/daily tracking, but I use Things for task management and move To Do’s from Things to Habitica when I want to prioritize them (or get XP for them, ha).
- Variety in quest mechanics. Yes, quests have different pixel art and descriptions, but they are all essentially the same, either boss battles or collection quests that are just a matter of racking up hits on the boss or collecting items. Why not combine them with specific tasks (like Challenges?) so there is some variety?
- More content to keep the engagement going. I felt a sense of completeness after completing the “final” quest (Lost Masterclasser) and dropped off the app for a bit. I think more community engagement could keep the app evergreen. In addition to letting people make Challenges, why not bring back incentives for people to write quest lines etc.? Reading the wiki it looks like people used to be able to get awards for contributing in various ways beyond submitting code.

Thanks again for the amazing app, really appreciate the work you are all doing!

title: I keep trying to like it
body:
But honestly it makes no sense. 

It’s not intuitive. I’m not motivated to do more because it’s not clear what the goal is or how I gain anything. Currency, mounts, clothing items, etc all seem to be random on what they require or how to obtain them. I honestly thought this entire game was microtransactions until I got into a menu where I in fact did have currency. I’m still not clear how items work or what to do with them though.

It says I get certain items for events on my notification but it’s not clear how to obtain them or if you’ve obtained them to equip them? It’s not clear how I can use anything this app offers as far as “rewards” to motivate myself at all. I use it as a checklist and that’s it. I set all my habits to monthly so I can see what I’ve done this month but it’s ridiculous when it resets on the first and there’s no way to view your history of chores. You lose a level if you run out of life. The app doesn’t care if you’re sick and has no option to really skip a day if you have another person to pickup dailies for you.

This app does nothing for me motivation wise and as much as I wanted it to work for my life it just doesn’t. Sunk cost fallacy is the only reason I’ve kept it this long. Devs barely tried and provide 0 instruction or direction to the player on how to even use the thing, much less how to customize anything or actually use it as a tool. Completing tasks does nothing, same with not completing them because the game doesn’t give you anything to look forward to or work towards. It’s really not clear what the goal of the game is and I’m not going to keep trying to figure it out.

title: They downgraded it
body:
Been meaning to review for a while. At first, I loved this app— it helped me a lot in college. But they removed the Guild feature, which probably wouldn’t be such a big deal if the guild I was in hadn’t been one of the most helpful aspects for me. I have ADHD, and I was in a guild that basically acted as a sort of support group where we could exchange tips or just share stories. Lots of us tried to message the dev team about how detrimental losing our guild would be, but every message was met with the same generic “we appreciate your feedback” corporate response. 
Granted, Habitica “relocated” the guild chats to Discord, so we can still communicate, but that meant having to go to a completely different platform to do so instead of having it in the same location as the other features, which is a huge mental roadblock for ADHDers like me. This led to me losing a lot of my motivation to use the app, and I’ve barely touched it since.

title: Works but the bullies aren’t worth it
body:
I really liked this app. I’ve enjoyed it and it helps. However, the players can be very toxic when it comes to parties. Recently I was bullied out of a party for not wanting to join a challenge due to my mental health. I can’t believe the things people will say to you in an app about self improvement (kys). Without the parties, this app is great but people are so cruel that my experience has spoiled the whole thing and now I just get upset when I open the app.
Developers response: I submitted a report every time. There are several different locations to do so so it’s very confusing. You also cannot flag on iOS and can’t report a chat once you’ve been removed. I submitted a fully detailed report to the suggested email and received a two sentence response saying we’re looking into it. Thanks. Lack lustre response. It doesn’t matter if I report. Nothing changes. And it doesn’t matter if I form my own party because you cannot tell how someone will behave before adding them to your party. It’s not a habit app. It’s a game. And the player base can be toxic despite what the developer says. I have screenshots that were never responded to. No support. I’m not using the app anymore. It just makes me sad. Back to paper and pen it is.

title: Good task management, nothing motivating
body:
If you were already planning to disrupt your life to build new habits and manage productivity, this is essentially a planner pretending to be a game. Could be fun. But it’s not enough to be a breakthrough solution for those of us who really need something different that works.

Back when I tried this app 10 years ago it had a social aspect where you could do challenges with other app users and discuss on in-app forums. Now at a time when I am really down to build new habits and stick to something, there is nothing actually motivating about using this app. Maybe if you’re a Cookie Clicker type and seeing the number of levels go up is enough for you, this will work. But there’s no social aspect and no unlocking of cool items—everything cool is behind microtransactions. Sure, you can earn rewards and customize a reward for your real life like watching TV. But I’m assuming I’m like most people this app is targeted for, who has little issue watching TV without feeling like I’ve “earned” it.

author: anjikaizen

title: ABSOLUTELY Awesome App!
body:
This app is Absolutely Awesome, If you stick with it long enough to figure out how it should work. It takes a bit time to get use to and figure out the point system according to your personal tasks, especially trying to figure out how to write dailies that won’t cause you to die to quick or barely do damage.
After using this app EVERY single day for 5 months and actually getting things done in my life for it, my only 2 asks would be for the ability to create folders that can hold ones tasks and the folders can be expanded instead of having to use tags and constantly have to click on and off to find and isolate my different tasks. Ive gotten really good at using the tags but folders would be 100x easier on my eyes and on my mind.
My second ask would be to have the ability gain points for each subtask that is completed under a task, as well as different difficulties for subtasks, and the ability to make certain subtasks required and others optional, because subtasks feel like something I use so often but are just completely useless in the way that they currently appear.

Ill end this with a few of my favorite features.
The ability to make my allocated points be distributed depending on the task that was completed is absolutely genius, and I love the fact that parties can do quests together, I only with the boss damages where shared between bosses.

My last piece of input is that I have contemplating many times in paying $9 of a party with the extra $3, but for some reason I only see that this offer is available on desktop and not mobile. I only wish there was maybe a video or something that could inform me on exactly what the offer contains and how it visually looks on desktop ASWELL as Mobile.

Over all, My Favorite app in the app store and I can’t see myself ever letting it go with how much more productive I've become.

title: Did not live up to the hype
body:
This was fun at the beginning, but it gets old quick because you are so limited in what you can do. You have to pay for a monthly subscription to even buy gems with the gold coins you win, and you have to pay to be on a team and complete quests with a party. There is not much merch to purchase with your gold, so once you buy all the weapons and whatnot, you just kind of stall out until they drop more stuff which is rarely…like 4 times a year. Also they limit the number of gems you can buy with gold to 20 a month and so you just kind of have to sit around collecting way too much gold (I’m over 1,000) with literally nothing to spend it on. 
You can buy seasonal merch but it does nothing…so I guess it’s a good game for people who like hoarding?
There needs to be more to this app. It’s like they thought of a good premise but just never actually took it where it could go. You just kind of have an avatar that you can dress and you win imaginary gold that just piles up…cool? The pets and mounts don’t do anything and there is no action. Not sure what we are supposed to be paying for with a subscription. Needs story and actual interactive content. Pointless after about a month. Very disappointed. 

I had such high hopes but my honest review is that this is just not worth it. Needs more design and content.

title: Literally Changing my Life
body:
TL:DR: App is literally changing my life at work and in my personal life. It uses social features and really simple design mechanics (sound, color, etc) to help you complete stuff. Highly recommended if you don’t mind the paywall. 

I want to say a big thank you to Habitica for making this app, because it’s actively changing my day-to-day life. I had been really struggling in almost every aspect of my life—especially work—to get done what I needed to get done. This simple app has helped me get more done in a few weeks than I have in months, and it’s genuinely helped me so much. If I can’t get motivated to do a task, I will put it in Habitica, and that alone will help me get it done. 

Some things I didn’t know when I downloaded that I think would have tipped me over sooner:
•You have habits, “dailies,” and to-dos. Your habits will change colors based on whether or not you do them *or* mark that you didn’t do them. This color changing alone has me 10x more likely to do a habit lol
•Your to-dos change color based on how long they’ve sat in your to-do list. They turn bright red when they’re not done
•You can weight the difficulty of a task

I find the “getting stuff” aspect of the app less appealing, so the paywall doesn’t bug me much, though if your main motivation would be getting pets/weapons/etc, I can see how it could be troublesome. The simple color-chancing mechanic of all the sections is really effective for me.

The guild feature is SUPER motivating, as well. I love joining in on quests with my guild. I just got a group of friends to join so that we could make a guild together! 

Love the app. God bless you guys!

The only things that would make the app better and raise my rating to 5 stars are:
1.) having the ability to set your own custom repeat durations (like 2 weeks for payday-related reminders or 28 days for refilling certain medications, etc.)

Definitely loving the ad-free interface and the fact that the free version doesn’t interfere with the app’s functionality. Even though the organization is a bit chaotic, it was still pretty easy to figure out.

title: A Shell of What It Used to Be
body:
Habitica used to be wonderful. The task manager itself is so-so and simplistic, but the community really helped me with accountability and growth. It was so encouraging and fun!

Fast forward: the staff have been slowly dismantling everything good about the app. The social spaces have been almost entirely removed (a core feature, disappeared). There have been no meaningful new features, so it continues to fall behind other apps.

The Pros? It’s free.

The Cons? It’s a sinking ship, and there are a million better apps out there for both productivity and gamification.

But the bugs are all over the app. When I try to post something to my Party, the app FREEZES completely, and I have to restart it.

And the thing is, those bugs AREN’T BEING FIXED. I’ve hung around the last few years, trying to like the app, but no improvements have been made beyond little superficial ones here and there. You expect people to PAY FOR THIS?? You actually have a paid staff of developers for this?? What are they doing all day? Habitica corporation: Do better.

Anyone else reading this: Find a different productivity app. You’ll be glad you did.

title: Productivity disguised as a game
body:
I’m in my mid 20’s and got into a mental slump when the pandemic hit and I was working a job that drained every ounce of life that I could give. The only way I could recharge was spending time with my friends, so that was all I wanted to do.

Since then I’ve gotten married, moved jobs twice to something that I now love more than anything, gotten 2 cats and a new, bigger apartment. But I still find myself in that mental slump of 0 motivation to do anything but be with people.

This app, this game, gave me real-time rewards for doing the mundane, rather than having to wait and see if or when my wife would thank me for doing the dishes or taking out the trash as needed. I had habits that I wanted to break (such as setting repeat alarms or getting back into bed after turning off my alarm and potentially falling back asleep). I wanted to do daily chores to try and get rid of the cockroaches that started to infest our apartment, as of 2 weeks ago, they’re all but gone. This app works if you find fulfillment in being rewarded for doing things, mundane things. I highly recommend this to anyone who wants to restart and have a valuable tool to do so

author: KDANETH

body:
I am a data scientist in my 30s and I absolutely love Habitica and use it with my partner. We both have elaborate wardrobes and can be found hollering across the house to come look at eachother's Habitica outfit despite having used it for like 4 years now. There are pay-to-play features but they are not absolute (there are other ways to access those items through the MMO community interaction aspect, it's just harder and less likely) and the basal experience is good enough. I didn't pay for I think the first year; it's $5/mo if you want a consistent in-game monthly income of the higher-tier in-game currency, basically. 

To summarize, you have your own content you can interact with, and other people out in the external Habitica world (you don't walk around on a map, you join groups and essentially engage in an automated tabletop RPG by completing your task list with the computer as the DM). It is 4-seasonal with 4 themed events where you can acquire items that may or may not recur. There is a huge, huge variety of pets you can hatch and evolve (one stage evolution) in any potion color (there are I think 7 basic and an unknown amt of special potions). This is my favorite part. 

The community is very active in improving the codebase and you can create and contribute objects yourself as a pixel artist, though not 100% of submissions are used / you have to get on github and get picked to make them (but it's achievable); there are in-game awards for this kind of contribution. 

I use it for managing my basic self-care tasks and simple errands as I have a chronic illness. Before I was a data scientist I also used it to motivate myself to study coding. There are both boolean valued (check-off) tasks and activities that you can claim an unlimited # of rewards for; you create them. You control this size of the reward you get for the tasks and there is a workaround system to adjust your settings (your gold and mana) if you mess something up or there's a glitch (I've never used this). You cannot alter your amount of the higher-tier currency, potions, etc. and must get a mod to help you if you experience a glitch there (this has happened to me one time, and it was because my internet was flickering in and out rapidly right at the very moment that the reward for the group tabletop-style quest was marked complete; I had other glitches in other softwares due to my computer's behavior so it wasn't their fault but they fixed it within 24hrs). 

Everyone is there in good faith. There are identity-based and task-based groups and a server-wide groupchat for interacting with mods on various pragmatic issues like previously discussed. I forget how, but I don't think Habitica hires mods, I think people become mods through a certain amount of community contribution (might be wrong on this); also anyone can start a group if you have a small amount of the higher-tier currency to put in your group's bank (but you can pull it right back out afterwards, heh). There is a group that goes around taking over and "robbing" the banks of abandoned groups and it has become Habitica-sanctioned, which I love.

Okay, this description is getting out of control. There's a ton more. It's really good. However the gameplay is NOT so spin-offy that it becomes a timewaster in and of itself; doing your tasks drives everything.

title: Helpful beyond belief, and such a wholesome environment!
body:
This app (and website) are exactly what I needed in my life. I joined about five or six months ago now, and Habitica has really helped me get my life together. I have ADHD and severe anxiety, and keeping track of what I need to do (not to mention doing it) has always been a challenge for me.

Before, I’d just make checklists on my computer or scraps of paper each day, but it was annoying having to essentially re-do the list every day (either re-writing it or unchecking the checked stuff that needed to be done daily), plus it was really easy to forget things that needed to be added to the list.

With Habitica, I can easily keep track of all my daily tasks, and even tasks that repeat but not as frequently. I can make tasks repeat every x months, weeks, or days, or even have things repeat on specific days (every M/W/F, for example). Repeating tasks and one-time tasks are kept separate, and I can add due dates for the one-time tasks. Tags make it easy to sort tasks/habits, and if I ever want to rearrange where things fall on my list, that’s a breeze too!

Fun quests and rewards make it easy to keep me going, especially with my habits. I’m very rewards-oriented, and there have been multiple occasions where I haven’t wanted to work on my habits but was motivated into it because I wanted to do more damage to the boss I was fighting. I was worried that I’d obtain everything possible pretty soon and then lose my motivation, but there’s so much to do and more comes along all the time!

Everyone on the site is so welcoming and supportive; it’s a very wholesome environment. I was scared to ask questions at first, in case people were mean about me not knowing/understanding things, but every time I have asked a question or read the Tavern chat logs, everyone has been kind, helpful, and supportive in everything they say.

There are things you can pay real money for, but everything is fairly priced and you can also access 99% of things without paying real money anyway. The only things you can’t get without paying real money are subscriber-exclusive items, which come out monthly but are really only cosmetic; they offer no in-game benefits other than looking neat. And there’s definitely plenty of neat-looking stuff without that, too!

Habitica has changed my life, and I am so, so grateful for all that it provides—to me, and to everyone else who finds it helpful in their lives.

Good luck, everyone! Whatever it is you want to be changing in your life, I know you can do it :)

title: Well...
body: I loved this app for a while, it gives you rewards for doing every day things and makes you feel like you’ve accomplished something. But then the gems. Gems are the in game currency you have to purchase with real money (different to gold which you can earn). Having to buy game currency is one of my biggest pet peeves. You can’t convert gold to gems, you can’t sell stuff to get gems, and it’s nearly impossible to get them. The only way to get them is to do “challenges” posted by other users which are difficult to do for 1-2 gems (which is not guaranteed. Some challenges only 1 person wins). Another way is to “contribute” which I have yet to figure out what that means but from the tings I have seen it is minimal pay out as well. I wanted to get all of the pets and unlocked all of the ones you can get through day to say activity, but “quests” take forever and rarely give you eggs to hatch so I have not gotten many of those either. The only way to get new potions (after the core 11) is to buy them with gems. Basically, don’t get this app if you actually want to unlock everything or complete quests and missions. I’ve had this app for over a year and I’m considering deleting because I’ve exhausted everything I can do

author: Daniel Thomas Scott

title: Great program, imperfect app
body:
I started out on the Habitica app, not knowing any different. Lo and behold in a conversation with customer service I discovered there was a web version (via the words “oh, that works on desktop” to something that wasn’t working). Desktop version is amazing! It’s social! It loads everything! You can be an obsessive pet organizer!

Habitica has been great at updating the app and it’s already loads better, but just be warned if you are downloading the app for the first time, it’s not perfect yet.

For instance: my laptop was stolen and I am changing all my passwords. I can’t do that in the app. Seems a little unsafe and quite a flaw. 

I’d love to report this in the app itself, but I don’t have email set up on my phone, so I can’t. (For the record, yes, this is an old-person problem, but I don’t want constant emails on my phone, okay? Why can’t you just give me the email address?)

Once again, Habitica is a great place and so worth your time. Just maybe don’t spend all your time on the app just yet.

title: This is the best thing!
body: First, three facts about me, for background:  One, I am a single parent with four kids, six pets, a bunch of house plants, and an extremely busy life.  Two, I have tried dozens of productivity and habit tracking apps.  Three, I hate video games and computer games.  BUT… this app is amazing.  It makes even my least favorite tasks desirable, it keeps me motivated to do things even when I’m exhausted, and it keeps me focused on what I need to do, even when I have a million distractions.  I probably never would have tried it had it not been mentioned in a New York Times article (not even about tech or anything like that, it was about a day in the life of a Zen chaplain).  I figured I’d give Habitica a shot, but with very low expectations.  I’m so glad I tried it!  It benefits me and every living being in my house every single day.  I fully recommend it to anyone who’s trying to build good habits and/or be more productive, even if you think it’s not for you.  Try it for a couple days, and I bet you’ll see benefits.  And have fun!

title: Top notch, would recommend
body:
I started using this app after reading a glowing recommendation on a ‘how to get things done’ site, and it has not disappointed. Much like the grownup version of a sticker chart, this app encourages the user to perform those boring day to day chores and tasks that we keep meaning to do but forget about. Some particular things I like:

- the fact that before rolling over to the next day, it will ask you what things you may have forgotten to check off the day before, so you don’t get penalized for ‘not logging in’

-the variety of categories tasks can be put in: one time items vs once a day items vs multiple times a day items

-being able to subdivide tasks into smaller sub take by using checklists

Some things I’d really like to see:

-the ability to send other members in your party a task—I feel like this would be especially useful for shopping lists

-being able to save or repost a past to-do. This would be great for those chores that are infrequent or dependent on some sort of irregular outside thing (the weather) but involve enough complexity that recreating could be a pain. To limit lag and storage this could be limited to saving up to 5 to-dos?

That said, all of this would be bonus material and I intend to keep using this app long term and recommending it to others.

title: Habitica can be a total Game Changer
body:
I’ve been using Habitica for almost two years now, and I’m here to say that as I was initially a casual  user of the app, and have moved to being a player in a world parallel yet decidedly different from our own. With Habitica being a highly customizable game, you truly can gamify your habits and tasks to suit your own level of creativity, utilitarianism, minimalism, and community engagement. The guilds are supportive and members are eager to give encouragement and feedback, and the challenges that the guilds provide are usually well written and sometimes use “RPG lingo” to make it more like a game and less like a chore list. 
I started changing the names of my tasks to “unlock achievements “ and my habit lists to “Activate power ups “ , and it’s been significantly helpful to keep my attention and engagement with the app. Furthermore: purchasing the app is going to be the game changer. While you don’t technically “need” to, it opens up another level of interest and engagement with special Pet and potion Quests, and Habitica gives you a bundle of items every month you subscribe, and a special little pet as a thank you. Purchases keep the app free and free of ads for free users. 

However, this month I found that the Mystery Gift items did not show up in my Items list. I’m wondering if it’s a bug

title: Inclusive phobia protection feature!!!
body:
I use the app with a few friends and it’s great for keeping track of habits and giving me external motivation - which I definitely need to make new habits/ keep up tough ones. 

I’m really excited about the phobia protection feature though. It is an add-on that will remove images of spiders, snakes, zombies, etc - things people may have phobias of. One of the friends that uses Habitica with me has a massive phobia of spiders and, while I think she’s ok with digital spiders, I never realized how apps I use easily (and invited her to use with me) might not be accessible to her during Halloween. I didn’t realize how important this kind of feature is for inclusivity until I saw it. I know how stressful the phobia is for her in person and I appreciate that Habitica is providing an option for people to avoid seeing potentially upsetting images when they’re everywhere during Halloween season. 

I just had to drop a review because this kind of feature makes apps accessible to everyone- as they should be. It shows me that Habitica has people behind it that care about other people.

title: Gamification done RIGHT.
body:
So many productivity gurus will tell you to “gamify” things in your life to get things done. It’ll help you stop procrastinating they say!

But if you ASK what they mean by that, you get vague terms like “reward systems” and “set it like an appointment so you don’t miss it”

You know what reward system WORKS? A HEALTH BAR AND A SKILL TREE

You know what “appointment” I never miss? My daily tasks on animal crossing and that sweet, sweet LoL match with my friends. 

Habitica brings the gaming experience to mundane tasks. 
Did you take out your trash today? XP!
Did you fold the laundry even though you hate it and would rather pull out you own eyeballs? MOAR XP!
Did you make that appointment with your doc that you’ve been putting off for 6 months +?! XP GALORE!

Join a guild or set up a party with friends! Get REALLY competitive with you avatar looks. It’s all in the name of XP... I mean... ADULTIN... I mean... PRODUCTIVITY!

title: Great app, but could be even better
body:
After becoming aware of my problem with IOS games and how much time i waste on them, I wondered if a game existed that actually encouraged you to be productive and improve yourself. I struggle with severe productivity anxiety and it really hurt my college attendance and grades, but this game has worked wonders!

There are some small improvements I would LOVE to see from the game that would really add to it!

1. You can score the difficulty of the tasks you would like to accomplish, which give rewards proportionate to the difficulty. I find that this game works the best when I set the difficulty to hard, as that’s the only real way that I feel truly accomplished and rewarded for doing things. I think the rewards should be even better.

2. Leveling up doesn’t really do much. You have to get all the way to level 10 to even choose a class. I need something to incentivize me to really really wanna level up.

3. I wish there was an actual game I could play with my character, like a JRPG style turn-based combat system. Your character DOES fight bosses, but you don’t really get to join them.

This game is really on it’s way to something great, but I’m really hoping for a big overhaul of content soon!!

title: Really Helpful for School!
body:
It’s ridiculously hard to stay motivated during virtual classes, and I think Habitica has been a big help! I have all my school assignments up on my To-Do list, which is really helpful for keeping track of what to do and for staying motivated in the middle of working on an assignment.

The main reason why I love it so much is that it’s ridiculously effective for me and it’s just what I was looking for. A lot of other habit-tracker/to-do list apps aren’t in an engaging format, and I delete them after slowly losing interest over the course of a few days. I didn’t have this problem with Habitica, because of how it’s part game and part productivity tracker. I’ve been looking for an app like this for ages, and I didn’t find this until my friend recommended it (and thank goodness she did).

I haven’t noticed any bugs, other than the occasional small bug that comes from not syncing with the happening on my computer quickly enough. Occasionally there’s an issue where I check off a To-Do list item or a Daily and it doesn’t change color immediately, but it’s no big deal because the color changes if I go to another tab and then go back to the original. I’m also not entirely sold on the idea of gems basically being only obtainable through money, but I can appreciate that the things they purchase confer mostly cosmetic benefit.

author: kiralux13

title: Can't imagine a world without it
body:
I've been using Habitica for years. And, let me tell you: as someone with ADHD, this single fact is actually much more significant than it sounds. 

I have struggled all my life to find an app (or series of apps and schedules and reminders and calendars and motivation to *just keep trying hard enough*) to keep my days together. Nothing has ever stuck aside from Habitica. I absolutely loved and still love the Moleskine suite of apps, but my chaotic, unfocused, and tired brain just can't do minimalism successfully. 

Habitica, on the other hand, is enormously flexible and expansive, perhaps even overwhelmingly so at first. That said, there is a large & active community of users available to give you ideas for how to use the app and also to encourage you along the way. The community truly puts other apps that boast a "social" component to shame.  

For me personally, I do use the app to work on habits I'm trying to develop, but I also use it for pretty much every other logistical aspect of my life: project management, collecting/bookmarking, reminders, delegation, and brainstorming. I would be an absolute mess without it.

So if you have ADHD or you struggle to keep everything together, I cannot recommend this app enough. Give it a try.

It’s fun, it’s simple, and it’s effective. I’m so happy there is a team that created this idea and put it into the world, this is exactly what I needed. I’ve been using it for close to a year now. When I’m having some depressive episodes, I’m able to pause the “game” until I’m confident in my ability to get back on my feet. Which is something I’m /so/ thankful for. No, I’m not a bot, and I have not been paid a single penny to say any of this. I just genuinely love this app so much. I wanted to show my gratitude towards the developers and everyone that participates in the making and improvement of this app, because it changed my life and I’m forever grateful.

body:

-Be able to choose what days you do your dailies on. For example, instead of choosing daily for my schoolwork, I can checkmark Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, and leave Sunday and Saturday unchecked, as I don’t do school on those days.

-A priority system that prevents spending coins until the user completed the prioritized task. Example: I set school as a priority that prevents me from spending coins on rewards if I don’t have that priority checked off for the day. It’s possible to make lots of money off of less important dailies, habits, or to dos and reward yourself without doing the other, more important and/or more challenging tasks. 

Otherwise, such a great app that really helps hold me accountable to the goals I want to achieve in a fun way!

title: Keep on track
body:
With the quarantine, me and my friends felt like time was fake, cause it is. My one friend found this and we all downloaded it. It helps us remember to finish all our tasks, and remember to do our simple ones. It’s easy to use, and makes us excited to find things to do. Its helping us actually get around to stuff during a really weird time. 

It’s basically a Dnd to-do list, but it’s really fun. The quests especially make me want to do the tasks. 

Now for some negatives, it’s an honor code. Technically nothing is stopping you from just checking stuff off, but that’s just a general negative with every to do list. The app is a little tricky to customize the character, specifically weapons and equipment. It’s a little out of the way, and you have to know where to look a little bit. The app is also a little slow to load, but if you leave the page and go back to your to-dos or your habits, it usually straightens itself out. 

I highly recommend this, it’s really motivating, and doesn’t take that much effort to set up!

title: THIS GOT MY LIFE TOGETHER
body:
I literally love everything about this app. It got my entire life together. I credit it for my productivity in every aspect. It really is perfectly tailored for the user. A couple reasons why you should totally get this app:

-The combination of ways to write tasks is soooo convenient! There are dailies for what you do on a repeated day to day or week to week basis, habits for things you want to do but aren’t quite doing every day yet, and a to-do list. This way I can keep “brush your teeth”, “keep your room clean”’ and “organize your desk” separated by appropriate category.

-The gaming aspect is AWESOME! With other apps you check something off your todo and then that’s it. No real reward. With Habitica I get excited to level up or buy new items for my avatar! Plus I can make my own rewards so I can buy myself set rewards like “go out for ice cream” with currency I earn by completing my tasks.

-With every missed daily or negative habit you lose life. This keeps me motivated to stay on top of things. But if I do fall behind, I just have to work a bit harder to buy a healing potion that can bring my health back up. I have to use the same gold that would be going towards my rewards otherwise, so it’s good motivation to stay productive.

Honestly, just give this app a try. It’s really worth it. If you’re the type to be motivated by games, leveling up, and earning rewards, this is definitely the best app you can have for this type of thing.

author: smoochking

title: Absolutely Amazing! Except....
body:
I love this app. Having that little ding sound whenever I complete a task is incredible. It makes me want to do my things so bad because it puts stake in it.

It’s fun, and relaxed, and all the guilds I’m in are so supportive! I’ve started doing things that I previously did once or twice a week every single day. I’m legitimately excited about completing my tasks!

The RPG style makes the whole thing a game, and if you love farming games like me (any Slime Rancher bois in the house?), it’s absolutely perfect because you’ve already got the app structure wired into your brain. It really works.

I appreciate the lower pressure option of habits versus dailies, which lets me separate out the needs and the wants. Make sure you don’t overstock your dailies!! Be realistic, love yourself, and remember: if you set the goal to high, you’ll come to resent the goal and quite possibly resent the whole app system that is otherwise so helpful. Be realistic. It’s ok if you can’t do everything. Baby steps!

Also, put everything in there. Even the little things. It makes such a huge difference to have every little thing that is a chore or needs to be a habit get positive reinforcement, because it makes me so much more excited to complete the harder tasks!

Now for the Except... 

My only problem? The sound when you click the plus for a habit.... it’s low, and honestly sounds like a failure sound. I hate it, and it makes me unhappy because my gamer brain doesn’t feel like I accomplished something, it feels like I lost a life or took a hit. It’s a low sound, and I turn off the sound every time I click plus on a habit because I can’t stand it and it makes me sad. It’s such a shame because the other sounds for success are so happy!!! Please, please change it. I did something. Good, and that sound makes me want to cry because it sounds like I failed.

I’m sorry, I know this seems like an overreaction, I just... it really makes a difference for me. 

Outside of that, this app is wonderful and I really appreciate it.

title: A habit tracker/motivator that’s actually fun
body: As a chronic procrastinator, I’ve gone through my share of apps intended to kick myself into action toward my goals, and nothing has worked as well as Habitica. It perfectly aligns my real-world goals with my insatiable need for collectible digital pets... I almost wish I was joking, but no, collecting virtual animals in this game has somehow been a more effective motivator than anything I’ve tried. Plus, joining a party and talking to other real humans with real human ambitions has really ramped up my motivation to be even more ambitious with my goals. A little buggy sometimes, but the app has a lot of heart behind it and despite occasional problems connecting to the server is still just an all-around delight to use. To the devs, thanks!

title: Wonderful App!
body:
I love Habitica! I have used this service off and on since it was created, but recently I have started using Habitica every day. I love the separation between Habits, To Dos, and Dailies, as well as the gentle character customization and the inclusion of a place to converse with other players. 

I have encountered bugs where my items will not be checked off until I do it a few times, or the app will lag when putting a new item. That is the reason for my Four Stars instead of Five. Also, I would really like if we could tag each task under a category, and be able to track that tag with the tasks we did. I think it would be nice to see how many times I checked “Clean my room” and not just as part of a streak. 

Overall, this app is a great way to keep track of your to-dos. Its interface is simple but effective, and works well for people who enjoy a bit of fun even among the mundane. This is not a full “game,” for anyone confused, but adds an entertainment factor, as well as a rewarding one, for those looking to be more productive. I have tried many productivity apps, and this is the one I consistently remember and come back to. Thank you for making this app!

title: For those of us who need a little extra nudge of motivation.
body:
This game is it. It’s adorable and easy to use. So your chores or projects or just daily habits you want to make routine are rewarded instantly. (You know us millennials with our instant gratification)
You might one day go for a run and pick up an egg! Panda, wolf, dragon? You may stumble upon a quest to complete with your friends, or you can just hack away at your own habits; either way it’s a great idea. 
This app has helped me immensely. I’ve always wanted to have a routine because humans are generally happier when they follow one. I just couldn’t force myself to do things like get out of bed before 9 or brushing my hair or doing my school work. 
I have moderate to severe depression which makes day to day habits that most people do without thinking a lot more difficult for me. Even things like just driving to the pharmacy to get my anti depressants. So if I find something difficult, I put it in my habitica list and it gives me an extra nudge of motivation. 
Five stars for sure.

title: Wow! So much potential!
body:
This app is everything I’ve been dreaming of. I used a Striiv as a teen and loved the garden game and being able to turn my physical activity into a video game. This app offer similar potential but needs some major work before its fully functional. 

1. I can’t scroll down in the challenges tab. I have a new iPad Pro and have yet to try on my iPhone. It’s frustrating i can only see the first few challenges, and when i scroll down as soon as my finger releases the screen shoots back to the top. Fix please. 

2. (Please don’t take this the wrong way bc i identify as a nerd too) and something us nerds do is hella over complicate things. I think if the UI was simplified it would make way more sense. And, issues would be easier to mitigate. 

3. It would be SUPER COOL if you could work with Nerd Fitness and get a thing going. If you’ve never heard of it look it up. I really feel like there could be a ton of amazing things of you worked with them, especially since getting healthy is a big reason why i, and others, are interested in the app. 

4. As an artist i would cream my shorts if i could use my own fantasy art for my avatar. Actually, I’d be willing to pay money monthly just for this option. Especially if you’d let it change it an infinite amount of times (some apps don’t, weird) so i could ‘grow’ my character w me. 

5. I haven’t spent much time in this app so forgive me if this i already a thing.... but... i would love if we could set personal challenges that only we get to see, Nd every time we do something for that challenge we see it as a percentage. Just thinking about my goal tracker on my browser and how great that would be in this app. Ex- a goal of mine is to read 20 books this year. Every time i read one i see it as a percentage, and it just really helps me motivate myself. 

I’d love to change this to a 5 star.
author: blinkofaneyeballs

title: Can you add (Goals)?
body:
Hello developers, I love this app though I wish I can add goals to my busy schedule. I think you should add another section similar to the others (habits, daily, to dos) and then right next to it “Goals”!   The goals should be able to be added anywhere and anytime. And the goals should be able to messed around with in the terms of the reward you get (coins and xp)  

For example,  I want to fix up my car and make it look nicer, and to do that I will need to do a lot of stuff such as: Oil change, New rims, new tires, clean the interior, wax my car, new steering wheel, work on the body, and just straight up detail my car.   I believe these fall under a different level of importance other than to do’s and habits. Mainly because I more than likely can’t get all those done in one day, and I feel I should be rewarded for those accomplishments...

For example,  “Oil Change” I rarely have enough time to get an oil change so I would put it in the “Goals” section and when I create that goal I will set the xp for 20 and gold for 100.   That way when I finally get around to it I will be rewarded for my sacrifice (Time and money).  

Not to mention making a “Goals” section would improve people’s motivation “ok oil change for 100 gold one step closer to getting a good weapon”. At least that’s how I feel. 

  Finally to the developers I took my time and patience from the day to write this to you so please respond or do something to let me know you saw my idea.  Also the app is amazing but I’m only putting four stars so you can see my review, thanks for your time

-Matthew Amperano

title: Habitica revolutionized the to-do app—now it needs to be one
body:
A thing I've learned about productivity apps—the less intuitively they fit your workflow, the more prone you are to fall off the wagon. I loved Habitica (then still HabitRPG) for it's brilliant (and charmingly nerdy) incentivization to stay on top of everything—and ultimately fell out of use because of a lack of a solid mobile UI (disincentivize).

Fortunately, it's come a long way, and with a much more intuitive interface on both desktop and mobile, it's a viable solution for everyone—not just those willing to make concessions for a killer concept.

The problem? Habitica's brilliant game-ified approach to the to-do list is hindered by its actual to-do list mechanics.

• A color-coded category system for home, work, etc (like is standard in most to-do apps)? Sorry, Habitica already uses colors for its "task value" mechanic. And no categories, just a rudimentary tag system. And sorting is manual only, (and because it needs to sync any single change you make before you can make another, it's an arduous process). Getting your tasks organized at a glance is not really an option.
• Push notification reminders for dailies/weeklies (Habitica's recurring routine tasks, which are separate from its one-time tasks)? They fire on seemingly random days, whether the task is due that day or not. Seems to be a bug some users have been suffering for months.
• Dailies that are due once every five days? You can do that, BUT: if it's the kind of task that, if you miss when it's due on Monday, needs to be done on Tuesday instead of waiting until Saturday, Habitica does not have you covered.
• Dailies that need to be done three times a week? Sorry, you have to specify which days of the week specifically.

Can they be worked around? Yeah, to some degree. But again: disincentives.

I understand the allure of Habitica is the game aspect, and as such, that's where most of the development resources go. But it's a little frustrating to see all the updates about special weapons and events when all the above issues persist, and start to have me keeping my actual tasks in 2Do (do you know how many dragons are in 2Do? ZERO).

title: Amazing App Gets Better!
body:
I downloaded this on a lark, with great cynicism, when it was recently featured in the App Store. 

While other reviews are fairly negative, I’d like to point out the following:

- This is an intuitive and *100% free* to play task and personal organization app. 

- Gamification of daily tasks, habits, and to-do’s is decently executed, with regular updates making the app better all of the time. 

- Development is ongoing and the Dev team seems to value user feedback a lot!

Bottom line for my 5-star rating is that I’ve paid a LOT to crawl through the bitter disappointment of the App Store’s organizational app category. This free app blows that all away and has helped me enact my personal time management goals. I’ve roped in most of my family already and it’s been great for managing house chore lists - we are just getting in to quests, which are a really neat incentive!

As someone with ADHD this is huge, so I highly suggest this for Neurodiverse folks - it’s free so there’s nothing to lose. 

TLDR; download this and give developers your feedback if you have complaints - otherwise it’s free, intuitive, and effective.

author: Disappointed mama123

title: Loved by teenagers & adults at our house
body:
I’m a Mom of six kids born over three decades (ages 2-21). I used to be an avid WoW player since vanilla, but quit now that I have 2 young kids again. I joined Habitica to use my love of video games to motivate me to do the many different things I have to do as a mother, wife, and homemaker.  I also suffer from chronic back & sciatic pain stemming from an L5/S1 herniated disc that has led to 2 surgeries & possibly more, and I've suffered from multiple mental illnesses for years. Habaticia is a sanctuary of kindness & motivation I'm so grateful to have found! It helps keep me accountable when my depression tells me to stay in bed all day, to socialize when my anxiety says to isolate, and to move and do something, anything, when my physical pain is high. I've shown it to my therapist and he highly approves and says he's recommended it to a few other clients! I'm also an autism advocate as 3 of my children are on the spectrum.2-21). I used to be an avid WoW player since vanilla, but quit now that I have 2 young kids again. I joined Habitica to use my love of video games to motivate me to do the many different things I have to do as a mother, wife, and homemaker.  I also suffer from chronic back & sciatic pain stemming from an L5/S1 herniated disc that has led to 2 surgeries & possibly more, and I've suffered from multiple mental illnesses for years. Habaticia is a sanctuary of kindness & motivation I'm so grateful to have found! It helps keep me accountable when my depression tells me to stay in bed all day, to socialize when my anxiety says to isolate, and to move and do something, anything, when my physical pain is high. I've shown it to my therapist and he thinks it’s great for me and has recommended it to other clients.

My teens and I are not only bonding with each other, we are improving our productivity as well.
Anyone ages 13ish up can use this. My teenagers set habits (positive ones to increase & negative ones to decrease), daily must (should) dos, and specific one time only to-dos around school, extracurriculars etc. We are all in a party together and we have friendly competitions about who levels faster etc. It’s silly that collecting every type of online cute pets is motivating enough to get me to clean or teenagers to do homework, but it’s working! We work on quests together it’s great. However you can TOTALLY play by yourself. I played for over three months before getting my family on board, and there are guilds, chats, and challenges anyone can join.
The community is probably the friendliest I’ve EVER seen on the internet, ask a question and you’ll get a friendly answer or pointed in the right direction. No hate, just a group of people looking to improve their real lives through a fun game. Many guilds covering a WIDE multitude of subjects, and challenges you can join to improve yourself further (I.E. I’m currently working on quitting vaping & keeping a cleaner home). Can’t recommend enough! The app does have its glitches, but the website version Habitica.com is near flawless with a very helpful Wiki the site directs you to. You can use the site and app back and forth rather seamlessly.

title: 10/10 IGN
body:
I don’t normally leave reviews, but I feel this app really deserves it.

Habitica, simply put, is a app that takes RPG elements from video games and applies them to real life duties in the form of “Habits,” To-Do’s,” and “Dailies.”  It’s a really interesting and fun concept; I’ve enjoyed it very much so far. I even spent the last hour coming up with achievement-like names for my to-do’s, dailies, and habits. While it wasn’t the most productive thing to do, I sure did get a kick out of it. To add icing to this already delicious cake, the in-app purchases are cosmetic only (as far as I know). Only complaint I have is that the raid boss is too OP. I’m kidding, haha. Kudos to the devs for making this wildly fun yet productive app.

author: AceQ262626

title: If I could bring one app to a desert island...
body:
...it would be Habitica. Ok, it would probably be Netflix or Youtube in all seriousness, but if productivity was more important than entertainment on that desert island, Habitica would be the winner!
Although the app is a little buggy sometimes, I've never had serious issues and there is usually a work- around (often as simple as waiting a few extra seconds for a screen to load). 
Habitica is the only app I open every single day, and I can honestly say it's changed my life. I have a list of about twenty Dailies, several of which are set to only appear on certain days of the week, helping me stick to some sort of daily routine (I didn't regularly brush my teeth, wash my face, or put on facial cream before using Habitica, and now I do them automatically! If that makes me sound like a slob...well, I sure used to be). They serve as reminders for tasks like practicing music, writing journal entries, taking birth control, and my "Big Three"--the three goals I set each day. Homework assignments that are due at the same time each week (like reading questions) are also a great fit for Dailies as they can be set for the day of the week that the recurring task is due. 
As for Habits, I try to curate that list more carefully, since the pressure of maintaining my "streak" isn't there to motivate me to complete them. I keep my list of Habits to 10 or less. They include "drink a glass of water," "write a book review on your blog," "meditate for five minutes," "exercise for fifteen minutes," and "do piano exercises." 
My To-Do list, by the way, is usually filled with Challenge tasks. (I don't create many myself.)
One of my favorite features? I can "dress up" my character using the "costume" feature, and collecting, raising and displaying pets and mounts is really fun, too!
Hope this review motivates you to try Habitica and gives you some ideas for all the different ways you can incorporate it into your life :)

I can open the app quickly to check off food bought at the store, give myself a little mental reward for following up on an email, or remind myself that it’s trash day tomorrow. I’ve gotten my entire family into it and now we play as a party, congratulating one another for staying on track! The developers clearly really care about the users and are always sending out cute updates about improvements. I played for free for a year until I had gotten almost all of the rewards and now pay the small monthly subscription to unlock the bonus materials. You can definitely play for free indefinitely and have a great time.

title: Don’t look anywhere else - HABITICA IS THE BEST!!
body:
Let me ask you a question. Would you rather be tracking your habits with no fun at all - no reward for completing your daily tasks? Or, would you rather obtain habits, daily tasks, and to-do’s but do them in the form of an RPG game, having fun while checking things off of your list? Well, the first option is every other habit tracking app in existence...and the second option is Habitica.

In Habitica, you can add habits, dailies, and to-do’s to your profile. When you complete these things, you gain coins, gems, and health. With coins and gems, you can purchase armor, weapons, pets, etc. These things will help you in quests, whether it’s a collect quest, boss quest, or anything else. You can also join a guild to quest with your best friends.

I love Habitica! I was recommended to it by a friend, and now I’m recommending it to you. It adds that little bit of fun that everyone needs in competing boring tasks that you usually procrastinate through and never get done. I’ve only been using Habitica for a few weeks, and I’ve already noticed TONS of positive differences
in my lifestyle. I realize that I am happier and more productive each day, and every night I go to bed feeling like I got a lot done that day. I definitely recommend this app to EVERYONE. I’m serious. GET HABITICA NOW!!!

body: I am so bad at getting things done once the day gets busy, but this app helps me work on habits and to-dos in a fun way. And to me one of the best dailies is the one that says “wrote 3-5 to-do’s for tomorrow” - that one gets my next day off to a good start before bed! There’s much to much to cover here but I love the app. The only thing I’d change is the ability to go on quests alone. None of my friends seems to use the app, and I don’t want to afflict a group of strangers with my unfinished dailies, but this knitter really wants a yarn pet - the quest scroll is maybe the second in-app purchase I’ve ever made!

title: Love it, but missing something very helpful
body:
This app makes setting and working towards goals easy, fun, and interactive. The only thing I would suggest as improvement would be to add an “Impact” option for each habit. For example, a bad habit that I set as high impact (let’s say smoking) would have a greater effect on my score than a bad habit with a low impact (such as checking email too much). The same with a high impact good habit (saying a prayer) compared to a low impact one (reading an inspiring quote in the morning). These would all have different effects on the score when completed or neglected, thus allowing the user to prioritize which ones to complete at first. 
Hope this suggestion helps :)

title: Love the app, but quality needs to be better
body:
Update: The latest 2 versions of the app have ceased to work at all for me. They crash on startup. The bug reporting link continues to be broken both on the web browser and app. As much as I love habitica, I'm seriously considering alternatives. I've worked through the cosmetic issues over the years because I love the concept, but it's just unusable now. 

I use this app all day long. Habitica has become a core part of my daily routine and in that respect, I love it. The mobile app however has had and continues to have quality problems that make it frustrating to use. The food for pets screen has had shown duplicates and "phantom food" for as long as I can remember, at least a year, probably more. Most recently, completing a task occasionally causes me to lose health?!? I totally appreciate the energy and I recognize that habitica is largely contribution driven, but if we want a larger community, the tools need to work reliably. 

Also, on a related note,the "report a bug" link on the website doesn't work from iOS safari.

Maybe it's time to up your goal!   Have an extra something to push for and having so that not doing extra doesn't hurt... would be awesome.   I know there's the habit section where you can plus or minus, but it's not the same.   Any way, cut motivating program and todo list. title: Punishment for Success
body: I was really excited about this app because it's about the only app that gives you a "reward" for meeting your goals, but I was dismayed to find out that if I maintained my habit, I got rewarded less. And you get rewarded more if you wait to get things done. So basically you get rewarded for procrastinating. There should be a streak tracker in it or something where you get rewarded more for maintaining a habit, but the rewards drop significantly as soon as you break the habit. There needs to be high reward and high stakes, and if there were, I would reverse this review. Instead, I'm just going to watch my progress grind to a halt and never get to level up because I am actually keeping my habits, which makes is discouraging  rather than habit forming

title: Good idea, poor execution
body: The app is fun. I enjoyed trying to get all of the pets and all of the armor. The task managing is slightly par albeit glitchy. The idea to gamify your to do list is a great one and I loved doing my tasks while I began using this app. However, the pet collecting begins to get old and not worth it once you've gotten them all in about a months time. While the app is a work in progress, I understand there will be some problems. However, in order to do 75% of the advanced things such as purchase gems with gold, change your name, or cancel a subscription, you have to use the website. This basically makes the app useless, as the app is only slightly faster than the website anyways. Customer support is also severely lacking, with one person in charge of the support that checks their emails once a day. There are many better task managers out there (that are also cheaper for a year subscription--ex. Todoist which is ~$30 vs ~$48 Habitica). Maybe in a year or two once the app has been smoothed out and the customer support has been taken seriously I will give it another try. For now, I will give other task managers a try.

title: Life changing
body:
Habitica it is absolutely one of the greatest apps I’ve ever used. I feel like video games (especially RPGs) have taught me a lot and helped me to become a productive grownup.

Habitica takes your every day task list and turns it into quests in a 8-bit RPG. The beauty of Habitica is there isn’t really anything to do except what you have to do in your day to day life. For example, you might set up a task “Workout"– When you complete it, you check it off and gain some experience and gold. When you and your friends start a “quest” you fight a monster or boss each night. Depending on how many of your tasks you did or didn’t do, you will damage the boss and/or he will damage you. You can also add bad habits in, like “Eat Donuts”, if you eat a donut, you click it and you will lose some HP that day. You do it yourself, so its basically honor system, but it wouldn’t be much fun if you cheated anyways

I love that each task lets you have a section inside that is a "checklist". This makes it so on the outside you can see "2/10 completed", which helps for larger projects. 
Honestly I recommend downloading this. If you end up not liking it the worst that happens is you have to delete it off you devise. But I don't think you will want to do that.

title: A+ method to staying on top of things
body:
I've been using this app for well over a year now and I'm still in love.

Perks of habitica:
- keep detailed lists of everything you need to get done, and have them repeat when you want them to.
- the different categories of lists make things SO easy to keep track of. I have flossing under 'habits', making my bed under 'dailies', and then schoolwork goes under 'to do'. It makes it easy for me to prioritize things and go from list to list efficiently.
- The gamer element to this app is what sold me completely. With quests that have mount, pet and item rewards, you feel compelled to collect them all (which I did and STILL feel hooked).
- The party and guild systems are a GREAT way to find similar app users to lightly socialize with and motivate yourself further! 
- On top of all of this, you can access your Habitica from your computer as well as your phone.

Negatives to this app:
- Bugs. Certain patches will sometimes lag or glitch, but this is a big app with many functions...so it's to be expected, but I'd like to see some server performance updates.
- this isn't so much a fault to the app, but I would like to see a button added to completely wipe out my inventory of items, as you just start collecting and hoarding them as you reach higher levels.
- Completely satisfied otherwise!

title: Love the premise & while slightly buggy, also has a lot of potential
body:
This is a very wonderfully made app - so, so useful! 
I love the +/- for the Habits section and the ability to add a due date on the To-Do list. The frequency & checklist option on Dailies is also super valuable to me. All of these functions just make this app so different than the other habit/productivity/to-do apps.
I would prefer an overview/abstract of how we're doing on a calendar and will probably fill out a feedback form to request that. As well as somehow adding the ability to set a dailies task that must be completed within, say 4 days, and if you miss the 1st day of that time frame, it doesn't just set it to 4 days later, it allows you 3 more days to finish and when you do complete the task, it'll set another 4-day timespan after - maybe by adding an option for hard deadline/open deadline?
There aren't any bugs that make the app unusable at all. There are a couple currently but they're minimal and don't take away from the usefulness of the app - it's just little dinks here and there like arrangement that bugs, at least in my experience. 
Thanks for such a great app and offering it for free! It's so great that the monetary parts of this app just gives inconsequential in-game purchases that are geared to the game aspect of the app. I don't really use the app as a game but the HP aspect does make me feel motivated to try harder! I'll definitely be purchasing some gems in the future to support the company. :)

title: Awesome Task Manager!
body:
At first I decided to try this app out in helping develop better habits with my email inbox and calling family, but I soon saw how much more this app can help me do.
 I tried a couple other task managers such as Todoist and Any.do before trying Habitica and none of them seemed to give me the features or user interface I wanted in a task manager even before paying for them. These apps sometimes put reminders behind paywalls, or made it cumbersome to set due dates or reminders. These apps also cluttered my list of tasks with other minor tasks I wanted to do eventually and didn't seem to have an unobtrusive or simple way to hide them for later. 
  Habitica on the other side has a simple label options where you can easily set a due date for some and none for others and you can then choose an option where it only shows you those tasks with due dates, puts them in due date order, and hides all other tasks, making the list itself a lot less intimidating. Habitica also offers the option of setting up recurring tasks and lets you choose the intervals from every other day to every month.
  What makes Habitica even more awesome is that they don't hide all of these awesome features behind a paywall, but have it all available in the base version unlike other apps.  
 Even if the idea of role-playing to do chores doesn't really appeal to you, Habitica works so well as a task manager that I'd recommend it to everyone, gamer or not-gamer. 
Awesome App!
