title: A party member's #1 pet peeve = vanished!!
body:
So, this app I am just beginning to tap into, since I have made it a slow but deep delving into gamifying my life and that of my family (that's Mama and two lil' ones...), it just corrected my most discerning of reviewers, my son Huxley Charles. 

Huxley said he'd accidentally press the (-) when he meant to press the (+) for habits and so he maintained a disdain for the habits. No matter what I said, he refuted my arguments with this seemingly small issue. 

I want to THANK you a million times over, because now our WHOLE family of three can use all main features. 

This app has changed our lives in the most positive ways. I want to thank my daughter Aurora Delphine because she did a cool thing I thought was meaningless at the start: making learning something new about Habitica a DAILY! We can go to her or communicate with Aurora Delphine, and he will tell us or message us something new every day that is a fantastic tip or trick.

We have very very little money right now, but I still bought gems to support because of the major contributions this program has made. We don't even need to make up our own prizes, though I have tried a little bit with that, because we realy think your avatars and mounts and potions are amazing.

Also, thank you for putting the number of "To-Do's" down in red as the Dailies have had. I have been involved in a few (about three) major projects that require an extraordinary amount of To-Do's and this assists in tempering that down a bit when I updated and saw I had "91", most of them due in the next 24 hours. Is it possible? Yes, I have pushed myself way beyond what I thought I could accomplish using these. And it helps I think to add small To-Do's you know you can get done quickly just to lower the number by three by adding five... if that makes sense! The boost I get self-esteem-wise is incredible.

I would like to thank the various Guilds and topics that encourage a person to turn something banal into something that sounds adventerous. I am currenty working on building the creativity of my dailies by doing this with every daily when it becomes possible.

I just now hooked up to the browser functions because I could no longer stand hearing about challenges and not being able to join them. I must say, the social support is there, the lack of structure as far as how many times you hit a (+) or (-) is there, and that gives you the freedom to judge yourself in a special way. It is helpful when I have to hit the (-) because I did a negative habit, but then based on howstrongly I decided and followed through stopping that habit, I will hit that (+) button. 

I have kept up to date on the research surrounding essential habits, habits that tend to have an effect on all other habits. In Habitica, one need not discover which habits are the essential ones, but simply organize life this way in whatever way suits you, and then you find things will indeed begin to go your wayand more positive habits will begin to domino from having some of the habits be these essential "KEY HABITS". 

I like the new icons; I like it showing the date for Dailies more pronounced there, and I can tell right now that my weekly shuffle of Habits, Dailies, and To-Do's will be a lot easier since the icons make me think of them more properly to begin with. 

I will have more to say once I have explored this more. But to our family, we appreciate the reduction in stress and the increase in the beauty of our bodies, our minds, our home, and our relationships. Even in the furthering of our education individually and as a group, and in the need for more social support from the shyest of us to the most outgoing, it has been ongoing for two days shy of two months STRAIGHT for the three of us: a 9.5 year old boy Huxley Charles, a just turned 12 year old girl Aurora Delphine, and a young Mama who has family and creativity proirities galore, that wuld otherwise BURST at the seams but for gamifying this way.

I will also mention that we are right now using Procraster and I am trying out learning IQTell.. we will have to see which email service is the best for filtering my email down to next to nothing (close to Inbox Zero would be GREAT!) and is the most user-friendly. I want to expand my knowledge of coding but that is through the kids who teach me. I hope we can all contribute to Habitica one day!

title: Platform for My Life
body:
As what I see as the love child of Fitbit, a classic paper planner, and Pokémon, Habitica has fundamentally improved the way I approach growth in life. It's fun, has an easy and aesthetically pleasing interface, and is both the goal-setting platform and planner I'd been wishing for for years. I've been using it for two years now, and I feel like I am so much more anchored on a day to day basis, I'm more confident in my ability to set and meet goals, and I'm much better at setting realistic goals that don't set me up for failure (and the frustration and self-critique that comes with it.)

Things I love best: 

Having a platform to set long term habit-building goals through the "Habits" and "Dailies" features. (That helps tackle the late-night random thoughts of "I should pick up the violin again" that I used to forget upon falling asleep, only to remember 4 months down the road.)

Keeping track of day to day things with the "To-Do" list (Sure, phone alarms and calendar apps work fine, but I don't get experience points and gold to buy rad armor for my avatar or food for my pet on Google Calendar...😜)

Enjoying the incentives worked into the game to make habit-building fun.(The aforementioned earning gold to buy equipment for my avatar and earning experience to level up notwithstanding, you can join up with friends or members of the incredible community to motivate each other and fight bosses [though you can do this solo too], and maybe my favorite of finding/buying pet eggs with your earned gold to hatch and enjoy as pets or feed to grow into a mounts.)

Many thanks to the incredible team that put together and runs Habitica.

title: Useful but buggy
body:
The concept is brilliant. I love getting points for doing the stuff I want to do. Getting penalized for not doing those things is less fun, but that's kind of the point.

The app is clever but buggy. It frequently reports a "Network Error" even when my Wi-Fi or cell signal is fine. I test the connection with other apps, and they have no trouble. The main problem with this connectivity drop is that offline, the app is useless. Usually apps store your activity and then upload when the connection is restored. But when the app can't connect to the server, you can't so much as tick a to-do item off your list. In this regard, it's often better to use the Habitica website rather than the app.

Another place where the website outdoes the app is in re-ordering lists. In the app, you can ostensibly press and hold an item to drag it to a new place in a list. For example, I like to keep my list of daily tasks in the order in which I do them, e.g., taking my meds in the morning and flossing at night. But this often doesn't stick, and lists get randomly disordered. So I tend to do the sorting on the website instead.

The benefits of using the app do outweigh the annoyance of these bugs. But only because the website makes up for the app's shortcomings.

title: Super fun, and life-changing!!
body:
I cannot say enough good things about Habitica! As someone who has major anxiety and Adult ADD, I've always found staying motivated impossible, and even tiny responsibilities often overwhelming. Habitica turned all of that around! With a clever interface simulating a 16-bit classic RPG, before I knew it I had the positive reinforcement I needed to turn my habits and responsibilities around. 

The goals are 100% customized for what YOU would like to improve about your life, but here's a sampling of my personal turn-arounds that this app has facilitated: my house went from being almost always messy (and kitchen dirty) to being pretty consistently clean, I've started eating better and losing weight, exercising more, getting more sleep, keeping better-informed on world events, saving and keeping better track of my money, and finally starting the process (after several years!) of applying to go back to school. Seriously, it's been a game-changer.

They recommend NOT starting off with goals that are too overwhelming, and I completely agree. As you progress and your character grows, you'll likely naturally want to make a few more life improvements (and get awesome rewards along the way!). Throughout the game you'll level up, eventually get to choose a class, get cool abilities and armor, and find eggs that hatch into a multitude of possible pets, which can often eventually grow into personal steeds!

It gets even better by forming/joining a party with some friends! You'll have help fighting bosses, being buffed by their abilities, and in real life, have even more mutual motivation to stay on top of the things that are important to you!

My only criticisms are that the app does not yet have the full features of the web version, but they are slowly integrating them! And in the meantime, you can always access your account from your phone's Internet to get that extra good
stuff. Still, just about everything you'll need is right there in the app!

I can't give Habitica enough praise. I highly recommend this app to anyone who wants to make some positive changes in their life.

title: Achievement Unlocked: Become a Better Person
body:
I can't say enough how much this app and website have changed my life. For the last few weeks since I got the app, I've been talking about it nearly non-stop... And for good reason. I've struggled for at least 12 years with self discipline and motivation, and no matter what, no organizational apps have been able to keep up with me and my needs. But this is set up perfectly to help me just the way I need. It gives me tangible things to work towards accomplishing, with more of a reward than the sense of accomplishment of checking something off. It helps me to see the progress I've made and break things down into manageable tasks, to sort them in ways that are logical to me, and to take hold of my life day to day as well as in the long term. I've nearly all but broken one of my longest standing bad habits, and the dailies allow me to make sure I'm getting done the small things each day that I might otherwise forget in the midst of a schedule that changes dramatically day to day.

The app doesn't have quite as much functionality as the website, in terms of not having quite as many little goodies, and there are the occasional glitches. But on the whole, the main functionality of the app, where the task management is concerned, functions exactly as it should, and that's what matters the most. I definitely recommend using it concurrent with the website interface, as some of the other aspects function a bit better there. But on the whole? The experience is incredible no matter where you use it.

I'd say this app may not be for everyone, but since starting to use it, I've gotten my family into using it, and they've in turn spread it to their friends... So that's people anywhere from their mid-50s to as young as high school all finding the benefit in it. So maybe it's not for everyone... But I think everyone should at least give it a try before deciding it's not for them, because the appeal is pretty universal.

title: If I could only have one fun app on my phone ...
body:

I downloaded this app before realizing it was the app version of a website. Turned out the website and the app are a terrific combination and have all the tools I needed to start building organization out of chaos. It is great for all ages and all backgrounds. People who want a fun way to keep track of daily habits and increase their productivity will find this useful. Those of us with ADHD will find it life-changing, and there are so many varied groups and communities within the program to lend a positive presence. Interactions and forums are well moderated, graphics are fun, rewards are creative, challenges offer incentives for positive reinforcement, and the community is welcoming and accepting. 

There are a handful of functions that aren't available on the app and must be done from the website, but for the most part, the app does everything I need it to do throughout the day. It even has the direct messaging function now. Truthfully, if I could only have one "fun" app on my phone, this is the one I would keep.

title: Habitica has changed how we do things
body:
Our whole family has been using Habitica for a few months, and it's made a huge difference in how we communicate.  I learned about it in an article about productivity apps and showed it to my 14-year old son, thinking he might be interested in something like this because he likes role-playing games like World of Warcraft.  He was so interested that I agreed to sign up with him.  To my surprise, I love it!  I never thought I'd have so much fun leveling up and collecting pets :)  But the best part is the social interaction - we now talk a lot more as a family about what needs to be done, what each person is working on, and what we want to do next.  We check in with each other every day, if for no other reason than deciding which quest to do next.  And we leave messages for each other in the party chat during the day when we're all off doing our own things.  Our party has expanded to include a few of my son's friends, my sister, and my in-laws.  We're all having a blast - the adults are having as much fun as the kids!  Just for comparison, I was a serious GTD-er before this, using Omnifocus and tickler files.  I still use those things to keep track of projects, but Habitica is so much fun for the smaller things!  I'd underestimated the power of fun in being productive.  And with features like tags, filters, checklists, notes, due dates, and repeating tasks, I can do a lot more with this app than I expected.

Additional note:  For me, the website is easier to navigate and seems like there are more features there, but I am impressed that most things can be done in the app...  I just have to look a little harder to figure out how to do it (like beginning a new quest, for example; it's apparent how to do it on the website, but not as obvious on the app).

Also, kudos to the developers for keeping things so active.  In the mere months we've been using this, there have been multiple app updates, a website update, a world quest (all Habiticans), special sets of seasonal gear and potions (turn your friends into flowers or starfish).  I'm truly impressed with all the details that go into this.  Thank you!

title: This app literally changed my life

Then I saw Habitica's ad with the rogue and the witch doing homework and yoga, and I downloaded the app immediately. To my delight, it is even better than I was anticipating. To my delight, I take that extra minute to send that last email, because in doing so I receive XP and gold! My productivity has increased drastically, and I no longer forget to complete tasks in my fast-paced work environment. I originally downloaded Habitica thinking it would be something I'd only use at work, but Habitica has also really helped me improve in the realm of self care. I now schedule those doctor's appointments. I reorganized that closet. I cleared out my wardrobe and donated lightly used items. I cooked dinner four out of five nights last week. I floss now. Yes. I floss. I am going to start meditating as a daily. And you know what? I'm actually going to do it. Because I really want to complete my collection of multi-colored, adorable
8-bit pets. I love this app. I recommend it to everyone I know. You won't regret this download. It changed my life.

title: Best GTD system I've found
body: I am a psychotherapist who works with youth facing ADHD and depression and I am promoting this app like crazy. For one, it finally gives socially isolated individuals a reason to take action on things. It's truly entertaining and reaches many who are tired of other people telling them what to do in life and how to do it. With this system, they do what they want for their own edification. That's huge! The second reason I'm promoting this app is because it is the best GTD system I've found for one reason: it is highly customizable to the individual's preference for 1) how to capture potential actions, and 2) how to be rewarded for taking actions. The power of the system is that it pays attention to both habit formation AND task completion. It is the complete behavior modification package. In addition, the game element is undeniably fun though it is never in-your-face and I don't feel childish at all using it. There are some bugs but give them time to work it out: the company is largely supported by an open-source, volunteer community. This is a true mom-and-pop organization. Plus, the app was originally meant to be supplementary to the website (though I haven't had the need to use the website). Speaking of community, the community guidelines ensure the public spaces are family-friendly and kid-appropriate. The website and app are most helpful when users interact with other community members, though this isn't necessary to enjoy the app and it may take some users time to feel safe enough. The community is very friendly to newcomers and all questions can be answered in the Tavern and guilds. TL;DR Best GTD system I've found because it's based on science and supported by a generous and kind community.

body:

RPGs really aren't my thing, and I honestly couldn't care less about the actual game aspect, but the organizational scheme, point system, and ability to generate your own rewards are features that are worthwhile on their own. Turning it into a game just gives you one more reason to actually use it!

I started with Habitica's desktop platform. I haven't had the best luck with list-based apps, so I was extremely skeptical when I downloaded it, but this is a beautiful and well organized interface. I will definitely continue using this app, and may even let go of the other to-do apps on my phone (I'm a business owner and a to-do list junkie). It's better than any of my paid apps. I can't believe it's free!

title: Awesome to do app
body:
This might be the coolest to do app I've seen. Completing tasks earns you gold and experience points to level up your little avatar. You can set up three types of tasks: habits (for positive/negative feedback), dailies (which you must complete in the specified time frame or they will cause you to lose health), and to do (which can be set with a due date or not). Tasks can have subtasks. You get to determine how difficult each task is, and you are rewarded/punished accordingly.

I gave it four stars because it is a little buggy (nothing that's interfered with using the app so far, just visual things). Also To Do tasks can't be set to repeat, which I could very much use.

title: Good redesign but needs fixes
body:
Love the new redesign! Looks very nice, flows well. As an iPhone user, however, I have a few big interface complaints which need tending:
-Drop down notifications within the app are very large, slow, and obtrusive. They cannot be dismissed, either, so multiple notifications (r.g. on login) are really annoying and interfere with use of the app.
-Scroll, scroll, scroll! Most interface list items take up way too much vertical space due to huge colored areas. This makes the app very inefficient when working with multiple items and prevents seeing more than two tasks at a time.
-Party and skills are buried in an irritating catch-all tab on the far right. Perhaps allow users to control which bottoms show on the bottom.
-Network lagginess. Combined with the aforementioned slow notification speed, makes using the app painful at times. Half the time, spell selection doesn't even do anything. Try logging in and casting two spells. See how long it takes!

title: I don't write reviews.
body:
I want to play this game. I REALLY want to play this. However it is extremely difficult to get into. Unless I'm fundamentally missing something to do ANYTHING rewarding in this app you have to be in a party, level 15, or buy a quest scroll. This makes the game very inaccessible to me, as my friends wouldn't be interested. That means I have to stick with this game long enough to get to level 15 before I can have fun with it. Are you kidding me? A good game design would get me hooked from the get go, THEN make me feel like I need to do real work to progress. 

For example what if the game started with a short play section. Perhaps a battle or an introduction sequence. Make it fun, I don't even know what I'm working towards. There's no reward that I see within my grasp. Oh coins? Uh... Okay. That I can buy weapons and gear with... Oooookay. To fight.. What? Why do I want this stuff? Why am I putting forth effort into this game? The concept is good but please designers, make me want it. You're giving me nothing.

title: Beautiful new interface to a great tool!
body:
Using HabitRPG has helped me improve my life.  I didn’t “get it” the first time I uploaded to, because thought of it as  a “to do” list.  It is much more than that.  For one thing, it’s helped me understand how I can make the changes I want to make in my life, and what keeps me motivated to do so.  It is a very flexible, intelligently conceived RPG that can become an essential tool to improve your life incrementally, and permanently.  

This new version is handsome, clear and a pleasure to use.  I love the new icon.  I had never thought of myself as a role play gamer, so the new name and icon feel more inclusive to me.  I prefer apps that have a sleek, visual appeal that this new app has.

To new users, be aware that the learning curve, even with the help of the tutorials, thoughtful game structure and excellent wiki, is still steep.  Not nearly as steep as OmniFocus, but much, much more effective, and much easier to use on a daily basis.  Start small and easy.  Get some wins.  If you get addicted, it will be to your own health and to the development of beneficial habits.

When you start using this app, you can (but do not have to) become part of a larger community of people trying to get things done, overcome bad habits or start good ones.  I’ve found this community to be very supportive and generous.  

Get this app, start using it, and support the brilliant, hard working developers.
